radiology_report:
Department of Radiology
UMCG (Groningen)
Date: 25 Jan 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 10.0 ng/mL, prior biopsy Gleason 3+4, suspected prostate cancer.
FINDINGS: Prostate volume 26.91 mL. T2-weighted imaging shows a focal hypointense lesion in the right peripheral zone apex. DWI demonstrates restricted diffusion with corresponding high signal on ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging shows early arterial enhancement. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion. No suspicious lymph nodes or distant metastases.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 5 lesion in right peripheral zone apex, approximately 12 mm. Prostate volume 26.91 mL. PSA density 0.372 ng/mL/mL. Clinical stage cT2a. csPCa predicted probability 0.8577571.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 7.0 ng/mL. Transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy performed. Pathology returned Gleason 3+4, ISUP grade group 2 adenocarcinoma in the peripheral zone, apex right. Discussed findings with patient, who expressed interest in further evaluation. Referred to urology for specialist assessment.

pathology_report:
Specimen: Transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy, 14 Oct 2024.
Microscopic examination reveals adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. Perineural invasion is not observed. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, apex right.
